discovery: Experimental discovery of the Higgs boson through the conception and construction of the ATLAS and CMS detectors at the LHC
motivation: The 2013 Prize recognised the theoretical prediction of the Brout-Englert-Higgs mechanism, confirmed by the ATLAS and CMS observation of the Higgs boson in 2012. The experimental achievement has not yet been honoured. Peter Jenni (founding ATLAS spokesperson) and Michel Della Negra and Tejinder Virdee (founders and leaders of CMS) conceived the general-purpose detector designs in the late 1980s and early 1990s, pushing calorimetry, tracking and muon spectrometry to unprecedented precision and radiation tolerance. They guided these detectors from concept to operation. Their detectors made two independent, statistically robust discoveries in the diphoton and four-lepton channels. Since then they have measured the boson's couplings, spin-parity and mass with growing precision. This established the first elementary scalar and completed the Standard Model. The same instruments now set the sharpest collider limits on supersymmetry, dark matter and extended Higgs sectors.
